target_customer: Remote and distributed software teams, paying per team or seat
problem: Remote teams lack the ambient awareness and spontaneous conversation of a physical office.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for a desktop virtual office app

founders.name: Rajiv Ayyangar
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Delectable and Aviate; TechCrunch (2019-08-20) lists Yahoo data scientist then director of product at Yakit. Later CEO of Product Hunt.

founders.name: Bernat Fortet Unanue
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him a former Yahoo employee. Left before the hybrid pivot per Ayyangar's blog.

founders.name: Tim Su
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him a former Yahoo employee.

exit.reason: Runway ran out in 2022; founders spun out an LLC and handed it to two team members to run as a small business. A sale process produced offers the founders did not like.

technical_complexity.rationale: Desktop app with presence, screen share and low latency video built on existing WebRTC style tools, plus integrations with Notion, GitHub and Trello; standard engineering for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: The founder says retention was poor and Slack Huddles replicated part of the use case; no data or integration lock-in documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Slack Huddles later covered part of the use case, which the founder cites as a reason for decline.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2019-08-20) reported signed contracts with Airbnb and Dropbox and 50% week over week growth at demo day. The founder later judged the viable market at about 250 companies and said many teams returned to offices.

branding.domain_note: Used tandem.chat, a .chat domain, not tandem.com.

rebrands.why: The company pivoted from a crypto portfolio tracker to remote collaboration, per Ayyangar's blog.

branding.community_and_virality: Fans gifted a blue tandem bicycle during the fundraise per the founder blog; demo day buzz and TechCrunch coverage; Product Hunt page with 189 followers.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong 2019 demo day buzz and a friendly real word name, but the name is shared by many companies and no sign of brand driven growth.

pivots.why: Per founder blog; remote work idea found after iterations such as Round Table and Wisp.

pivots.to: Hybrid Spaces hardware for hybrid work
pivots.why: Chasing return to office demand; the pivot used the remaining runway with almost no sales.

outcome_analysis: Tandem raised a $7.5M seed led by a16z in 2019 and rode demand for remote tools in 2020, but retention was poor and the founder judged the market to be about 250 companies. Slack Huddles and return to office policies cut demand, and a hybrid hardware pivot consumed the runway without sales. In 2022 the team spun the product into an LLC for two employees, and the product still runs while YC lists it Inactive.
notes: TechCrunch said the seed had not closed and reported a valuation above $30M from sources, so post money is left null; the founder blog confirms a $7.5M seed led by a16z. Seed investors beyond a16z (Shasta, Y Combinator, Liquid 2) come from a search summary of an aggregator and Crunchbase style listing. The $200K pre-seed rests on one aggregator (Employbl) and is undated. Totals vary: $7.5M versus $8.83M over 3 rounds, so a later round may be missing. tandem.chat page content could not be read (title only). Competitors left empty because the sources found (Pragli 2020-03, Teamflow, Slack Huddles) post-date the batch by more than a few months or are undated. A different Tandem raised $6.1M in 2025 and is excluded. Exit type is unknown because the product continues under an LLC while YC says Inactive.
